newsitem.title: USA: Childtime Learning sees Q2 below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Childtime Learning sees Q2 below estimates.

text.p: Childtime Learning Centers Inc said Monday earnings for the fiscal second quarter ended October 11 will be slightly below analysts' estimates, but will exceed last year.
Revenues for the second quarter will be nearly 20 percent above last year, it added.

Childtime President Harold Lewis said the shortfall in anticipated earnings is due to softer than expected fall enrollment in certain regional markets and the costs associated with bringing on 10 additional centers during the second quarter.

"We expect these same issues to affect the entire third quarter, resulting in net earnings which are expected to be lower than analysts' estimates and slightly below last year's pro forma results," Lewis said.
Fourth quarter earnings, however, are expected to be in line with analysts' current expectations as the company benefits from stronger than anticipated center growth, he added.
"Our next major enrollment begins in January 1997, and we are optimistic that trends will return to a more normal level," he added.
Childtime said it expects to announce actual second quarter results on or about November 20.

Childtime, the fifth largest child care provider in the United States, did not release current estimates for the second, third and fourth quarters. A company spokesman deferred to an analyst, whose estimates were not immediately available.
According to First Call, the mean estimate for the second quarter is $0.14 a share. The company spokesman said its pro forma earnings for the 1995 second quarter amounted to $0.12 a share.
The spokesman said pro forma year-ago earnings were $0.14 for the third quarter and $0.21 for the fourth quarter.
